author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing serves a page number below 1 as the first page
summary: Requesting the owner listing with a page number of 0 or below shows the first page of the listing with HTTP 200 instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a page number of 0, when the owner listing is requested, then the response is HTTP 200 and shows the same first page as a request for page 1
given a negative page number, when the owner listing is requested, then the response is HTTP 200 and shows the same first page as a request for page 1
non_goals: page numbers past the last page: the intake does not state a behavior for them
non-numeric page values: the intake does not state a behavior for them
any change to the search matching rules of REQ-OWN-002
notes: Intake source: handoff.jsonl line 1 (author human). Scope quotes: 'any page value below 1' and 'treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal listing (HTTP 200)'. test_names: one data-driven test whose rows are page 0 and a negative page, both against the page-1 listing. Observed cause, from the dispatch context and not a design decision: the requested page minus one reaches the page-request factory, which rejects a negative index. docs/architecture-principles.md classes clamping a request parameter to its permitted range as binding, which places it in the web controller. PRD edit: REQ-OWN-005 added to Owner records (narrative sentence, anchor, one Done-when bullet). No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by docs/architecture-principles.md Web controller row (normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding and belongs in the controller) and the OwnerController Contracts row in docs/system-design.md, which now lists REQ-OWN-005. No new module, type, or pattern. Basis: grep of OwnerController.java (processFindForm binds @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page; findPaginatedForOwnersLastName passes page - 1 to PageRequest.of, which rejects a negative index). IDE oracle not connected, so the grep is the weaker basis. Fix: clamp page to a minimum of 1 once at the top of processFindForm, and use the clamped value for both the repository query and the currentPage model attribute, so a request for page 0 or a negative page produces the same model as page 1.
integration_points: Framework transport: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch and @RequestParam binding (the sanctioned mock in CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Repository boundary: the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository stub in OwnerControllerTests. A framework stub is used because this @WebMvcTest fixture already wires it, and swapping in a hand-written double would restructure the whole class beyond this slice. Mockito is tolerated per docs/testing-principles.md. Assert the requested Pageable has page index 0 and that the currentPage model attribute is 1 for each row (page 0, a negative page).
Binding: no new entry point. The existing GET /owners handler keeps its current binding of the page int and the Owner search form.

risks.risk: The page parameter is clamped for the query but the raw value still reaches addPaginationModel, so currentPage renders 0 or a negative number and the pagination links differ from the page-1 response.
risks.mitigation: Clamp once and pass the single normalized value to both the query and the model (architecture-principles Web controller row: normalization is binding).

risks.risk: The owner listing path scales with the number of owners. docs/system-design.md has no Scale and Load section, so this path has no row to cite.
risks.mitigation: The slice adds no path and does not change the fixed page size, so the query stays bounded at one page per request. Simplest readable form. The missing section is flagged in notes for the design owner rather than added in this slice.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Design-doc write: REQ-OWN-005 added to the OwnerController Contracts row only. Out of scope and not to be folded in: VetController.findPaginated has the same page - 1 pattern and fails the same way for page values below 1. The slice names only the owner listing, so the vet listing is left unchanged and is a candidate for a separate requirement. Brief gap: docs/system-design.md lacks the Scale and Load section that design-validation reads. It should be added on a slice that adds a path that scales with data.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Input validation: the `page` query parameter is clamped before use (OwnerController.java:97 `int page = Math.max(requestedPage, 1);`). That clamped value reaches both PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) (OwnerController.java:136) and the `currentPage` model attribute, so a value of 0, a negative number, or Integer.MIN_VALUE can no longer raise the IllegalArgumentException that the exception-message-rendering error page would show (docs/system-design.md:206). The change narrows an error surface and opens none.

No check removed or weakened: the @InitBinder `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` (OwnerController.java:61) and the Owner binding on the search handler are unchanged, the lastName strip-and-prefix query path is untouched, and the int-typed binding still rejects non-numeric input through Spring's type conversion.

Upper bound unchanged and pre-existing: a large page value yields an empty or out-of-range Spring Data page (a long offset, no int overflow in the query) and adds no new sink. The new test is a MockMvc-driven controller test and adds no production surface.

Pattern sweep: `grep -rn -F -e "int page" -- src/main/java` found the same unclamped pattern in VetController.java:45 `showVetList(@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page, Model model)`. It predates this slice, sits outside REQ-OWN-005's owner-listing scope, and causes a bounded error-page response, not a security exposure, so it is not raised against this change.

Secrets and supply chain: the diff adds no credentials or secret-like literals and changes no dependencies. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (no match in build.gradle), so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: spring-boot-starter-webmvc 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind (tools.jackson) 3.1.5, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.
Docs changes (prd.md, system-design.md) only add requirement text and traceability IDs, with no security-context or threat-model change.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner listing page number to a minimum of 1

blast_radius.note: One production method in OwnerController.processFindForm gains a single clamp line and a renamed parameter, plus one new controller test and two traceability-only doc edits; no sensitive paths, one module, and no other route touched.

semantic_surprise.note: I read the hunk: Math.max(requestedPage, 1) is applied once and the clamped page feeds both PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5) and the currentPage model attribute, so it also handles Integer.MIN_VALUE. The explicit name = "page" keeps the bound query parameter unchanged after the rename, the default stays 1, and pages of 1 and above behave exactly as before.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized MockMvc test (rows 0 and -1) stubs the repository only for the exact first-page Pageable and asserts HTTP 200, the list view, and currentPage == 1. Without the clamp, PageRequest.of(-1, 5) throws and the test fails, so it exercises the changed boundary rather than restating the implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved and the cited lines I checked resolve (OwnerController.java:61, :97, :136; OwnerControllerTests.java:158, :161). The test-reviewer's round-two approval still carries a recommendation: the test's ownersPerPage = 5 mirrors the production page size, so changing that size breaks the exact-argument stub. The protocol counts a late-round recommendation as a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: The change matches the intake's bug report and the design-block's prescribed clamp. No design revisions, consultations, or build retries. The fix round touched only the test, and the out-of-scope VetController has the same unclamped pattern, which the security reviewer noted as pre-existing and left alone.

rationale: The production fix is a correct one-line clamp, and its test fails without the clamp. The only flag is the test-reviewer's residual recommendation that the test hardcodes the page size of 5. Read the test hunk, decide whether that coupling is acceptable, and note that VetController still has the same unclamped page parameter as a possible follow-up.
